description: The top-block value is CONCAVE in the displacement vector -- every internal term is -eps(2d + (u_i - u_j)), concave composed with a linear map; every bulk tail is -eps(2d + u_i); the cost is -(ln q0/2) sum u^2 -- so maximising it over real u >= 1 is a concave program, a relaxation of the integer problem and hence a rigorous upper bound.  Its value B_relax = 2.2537 is 1.042x the integer maximum where #7349's B_sharp was 1.816x, and the resulting cut on the e_inf search falls from 90 to 27, which IS enumerable (~6e6 blocks) where 90 (~1e10) is not.  An intermediate Jensen bound is also recorded: valid, 2.6951 over the measured T range, cut 43, still not enumerable.  The concave maximum is then CERTIFIED rather than merely converged: the supergradient inequality at the polished ascent point, with the linear term maximised over the per-row box the incumbent forces, closes with slack 6.4e-12 -- 6.8e-11 of the distance to the integer maximum.  The join over the certified cut reproduces #7335's independently searched e_inf = 2.43929645512078402706542884314 to 1e-30, at (s_t, s_b) = (8, 8).  Gap G2 is CLOSED at the run's measured block-length range; covering EVERY admissible length additionally needs REV_BLOCK_SUP_TMAX set to the rigorous T0 (the default 12 does not).  G1 -- Xbot(s) <= Xblock(s) -- is untouched and is now the only conditionality left on e_inf.

constants._note: the suprema are over T <= T_measured_max, NOT over all T.  T0_rigorous is the length past which the per-row cap forbids reaching B_certified; a run with T_measured_max >= T0_rigorous covers every admissible length and sets all_lengths_covered.  B_certified is the RIGOROUS number -- B_relax is the coordinate-ascent value, which is a lower bound on the sup, not an upper one.

certificate_P8.form: F concave => F(u) <= F(w) + grad F(w).(u - w); the per-row bound confines each u_i to [1, U_i] for any u reaching the incumbent, and the linear term is maximised over that box
certificate_P8.gradient: analytic (gx = -eps' in closed form), NOT a finite difference
certificate_P8._trap: the boundary rows carry strictly negative gradients at u = 1 (correct KKT).  Charging every row |g_i|(U_i - w_i) instead of g_i(1 - w_i) inflates the slack to the figure above and destroys the result.  Made here first; the figure is recomputed every run rather than quoted.

relaxation_P5.objective: Xblock(u) at real u, exactly -- no linearisation, no Jensen

jensen_P3.form: sum_i f(Delta_i) <= (T-d) f(mean),  f(x) = eps(2d) - eps(2d+x) concave

open_gaps.G2_status: item (a) CLOSED; item (b) needs REV_BLOCK_SUP_TMAX=40 (this run used 12)
open_gaps.G2_b: block lengths T = 1..40 exhaust the admissible range; this run measured T <= 12, so T = 13..40 is uncovered HERE.  A REV_BLOCK_SUP_TMAX=40 run declines monotonically at ln q0/2 per step from the T = 7 peak 2.25373 through 1.45889 (T=25), 0.98942 (T=34) and 0.67639 (T=40=T0), a factor of 3.33 below the peak
open_gaps.G1: unchanged and now the ONLY conditionality on e_inf: Xbot(s) <= Xblock(s) for every s, measured equal for s <= 12 and top-higher by 0.01982 at s = 13
open_gaps.headline: still the upper bound on M_n, which none of this touches

checks.name: P1 the real-u objective is the same function the integer enumeration maximised
checks.detail: F at the integer argmax reproduces #7349's enumerated maximum to -2.761e-30, and the Lambert tail resummation agrees with the direct sum to 3.155e-30 at 5 points.  Both matter: the relaxation is only a relaxation of the right problem if the extended function restricts correctly, and every evaluation here routes through the resummed tail rather than the sum #7349 used

checks.name: P2 the block value is concave in u — measured, not assumed
checks.detail: minimum concavity gap 0.00147382 over 200 random ordered triples.  The reason is one second derivative used three times: every internal term is `-eps(2d + (u_i - u_j))` up to a constant — concave composed with a linear map — every bulk tail is `-eps(2d + u_i)`, and the cost is `-(ln q0/2) sum u_i^2`.  This is what makes the relaxation to real u a CONCAVE PROGRAM rather than a search, so a coordinate-wise stationary point is the global maximum and not a local one

checks.name: P3 Jensen is a valid upper bound and saturates where the linear one runs away
checks.detail: 0 violations over 8 blocks.  The difference in kind shows at [8]: exact -1.1490916, Jensen -1.1490916 — equal, because a single-row block has no internal pairs and Jensen leaves the tail exact — against the linear bound's 2.8776793.  The linear bound claims a block worth MINUS one is worth nearly three, which is the whole of why B_sharp is 1.8x too big

checks.name: P4 B_sharp's slack is concentrated in row 0, and it is a missing cap
checks.detail: row 0's budget 2.893607227 is 73.79 % of B_sharp = 3.92139923, and it is attained at u_0 = 7.44745.  The true best single-row block is [3] at 0.9296691034 — 3.1125x less.  The per-row bound is the tangent at u = 0 and has no cap; the real gain saturates at S_e(1) = 2.568028 and then loses to the quadratic cost.  So the fix is not a better constant, it is a bound that bends

checks.name: P5 the relaxed sup is 1.04x the integer maximum, against B_sharp's 1.82x
checks.detail: B_relax = 2.2537313388386045641 at T = 7, argmax [3.9769, 2.794, 2.075, 1.5824, 1.231, 1.0, 1.0] — recognisably the integer argmax [4, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1] with integrality let out.  That is 1.04349x the integer maximum 2.15980237612, where B_sharp was 1.81563x.  The AP ordering constraint was DROPPED from the program (a further relaxation, so the bound stays valid) and the optimum satisfies it anyway at every T: True

checks.name: P6 the relaxed bound turns the cut from unenumerable into enumerable
checks.detail: B_sharp cut at 90 (~1e10 blocks, hopeless); B_jensen at 43; B_relax at 27, which is 6,325,874 blocks — minutes, not geological time.  Inside any such cut the enumeration carries no effective cap, since entries >= 1 and sum <= L force length <= L and every entry <= L.  So the ARITHMETIC of an unconditional closure now works; what is missing is the certificate, not the compute

checks.name: P7 block length is rigorously bounded
checks.detail: every row past index 5 contributes at most `Ghat(i+1) - ln q0/2 < 0`, so the cumulative per-row cap falls below the certified B_cert = 2.253735567 at T0 = 40: no block of length > 40 can reach it.  This run measured T <= 12, where the sup peaks at T = 7 and falls monotonically after — so T = 13..40 is UNMEASURED here.  Re-run with REV_BLOCK_SUP_TMAX=40 to cover it; that is compute, not insight, and the T <= 40 run declines monotonically at ln q0/2 = 0.05217036 per step throughout

checks.name: P8 the concave maximum is certified, not merely converged
checks.detail: the supergradient inequality at the coordinate-ascent point, with the linear term maximised over the per-row box the incumbent forces, gives sup F(T = 7) <= 2.25373556700090488296611 with slack 6.4265742e-12 — 6.84164e-11 of the distance to the integer maximum, so the certificate costs essentially nothing against the ascent value 2.2537313388386045641.  The gradient is ANALYTIC (`gx = -eps'` in closed form), not a finite difference.  The boundary rows are the whole difficulty: at the optimum the last rows sit at u = 1 with strictly negative gradients, which is correct KKT behaviour, and charging every row |g_i|(U_i - w_i) rather than g_i(1 - w_i) would inflate the slack to 1.4469556 — a factor of 2.25152e+11, enough to swamp the result many times over.  That error was made here first, and this figure is recomputed every run rather than quoted

checks.name: P9 the certified cut reproduces #7335's e_inf
checks.detail: the certificate's cut is s_t + s_b <= 27, 6,325,875 blocks, and the join over that window returns 2.43929645512078402706542883973 at (s_t, s_b) = (8, 8) with top block [3, 2, 1, 1, 1] — agreeing with #7335's independently searched 2.43929645512078402706542884314 to -3.41025e-27.  The block supremum over the same window is 2.159802376118285961604 at s = 14, comfortably under B_cert = 2.253735567000904883, so the cut is not merely large enough by luck.  This is the payoff: #7335's value was a search result, and inside the certified window it is a MAXIMUM — conditional now only on G1, not on how far the search happened to run

verdict: Concavity of the block value turns sup_s Xblock from a search into a concave program, shrinking gap G2 from 1.82x to 1.04x and the e_inf cut from an unenumerable 90 to an enumerable 27; the supergradient certificate then makes that maximum rigorous with slack 6.4e-12, and the join over the certified window returns #7335's e_inf exactly.  So e_inf is no longer 'the best value a search found' but the maximum over a window proved to contain it -- conditional on G1 alone.  The certificate's own trap is recorded and recomputed every run: the KKT boundary rows carry negative gradients and must be charged at u = 1, not at their box ends, or the slack inflates by eleven orders of magnitude.
